title: Valley-controlled chiral magnetism in transition metal dichalcogenide monolayers
authors: Igor S. Krivenko, Vladimir N. Mantsevich, Dmitry S. Smirnov
abstract: We put forward the Ruderman-Kittel-Kasuya-Yosida (RKKY) interaction in transition metal dichalcogenide monolayers as a tool to create and control a chiral magnetic texture. We show that in the spin-valley locking regime, the RKKY interaction acts as a Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya coupling with an effective spin rotation period exactly equal to the tripled lattice constant. Using mean field theory and classical Monte Carlo simulations, we demonstrate that this interaction qualitatively reshapes the phase diagram of atomically thin antiferromagnets. It destroys the chirality-related phase transition by selecting a single chirality value even when the RKKY interaction is small. At the same time, it shifts the Berezinskii-Kosterlitz-Thouless transition associated with spins orientation to higher temperatures. We argue that the valley degree of freedom of electrons mediating the RKKY interaction provides a powerful control knob for exploring non-universal phase transitions and quantum spin liquid states in two-dimensional van der Waals heterostructures.
summary: This work investigates how the Ruderman-Kittel-Kasuya-Yosida (RKKY) interaction, mediated by valley degrees of freedom in TMD monolayers, controls chiral magnetism. Using theoretical modeling and simulations, the authors show that this interaction fundamentally alters the magnetic phase diagram, stabilizing a unique chirality state while shifting the characteristic spin transition temperature.
main_problem: To use the RKKY interaction mediated by valley degree of freedom in TMD monolayers to create and control chiral magnetic textures, exploring non-universal phase transitions.
main_result: The chiral RKKY interaction reshapes the phase diagram by suppressing the chirality-related second-order transition while shifting the Berezinskii–Kosterlitz–Thouless (BKT) spin orientation transition to higher temperatures.
method: Mean field theory and classical Monte Carlo simulations are employed to analyze the system's phase diagram and critical behavior.
model_or_system: The study focuses on atomically thin TMD monolayers with localized magnetic moments, modeled by a Hamiltonian incorporating RKKY exchange ($H_{	ext{RKKY}}$) and direct exchange ($H_{	ext{dir}}$). The physics is governed by spin-valley locking in the low-energy electronic structure.
key_observables: Average chirality ($\langle\chiangle$), Berezinskii–Kosterlitz–Thouless (BKT) transition temperature, and specific heat capacity ($c_V(T)$).
important_parameters: RKKY interaction strength ($	ilde{V}$), direct exchange coupling ($J$), and the lattice structure parameters.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on mean-field theory for initial transition estimates, and Monte Carlo simulations are used to refine results, though approximations regarding the RKKY range are noted.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the chiral magnetic state (e.g., $120^\circ$ Néel state), temperature dependence of average chirality showing suppression by RKKY, and heat capacity peaks demonstrating BKT transition shifts.
paper_structure: The paper develops the Hamiltonian using second-order perturbation theory for the RKKY interaction in TMDs. It then applies mean field theory to analyze the chiral phase transition ($T_c$) and uses Monte Carlo simulations to study the spin orientation transition (BKT) as a function of RKKY strength.
why_interesting: The coupling between valley physics, long-range interactions (RKKY), and magnetic ordering provides a rich platform for studying emergent quantum phases beyond simple Heisenberg models, relevant to correlated electron systems.
